heading: 1. Corpus layout
why: Readers find the data (and only the data) in the same place in every corpus.

heading: 2. Works schema
why: Any reader can rely on the OpenAlex column names and types; extra columns cannot collide.

heading: 3. `_dataset.json` — dataset marker
why: The folder is recognisable as a corpus and says who wrote it and how its ids look.

heading: 4. `_query.json` and `_query.html` — per-query provenance
why: Every partition says how its records were obtained; methods sections can cite it.

heading: 5. Identifiers
why: Ids from different writers never collide and can be matched across corpora.

heading: 6. Package requirements
why: Packages can be installed and tested together and their output checked automatically.

heading: 7. Link table
why: Relations between records are read the same way for every corpus.

heading: 8. Analysis and processing packages
why: Packages that read corpora work with every compliant corpus and leave inputs untouched.
openalexAPI is the reference reader: a corpus it cannot read is not usable in the ecosystem.
